name: First Key Consulting
ai_use_case: advising brewers on data infrastructure and AI for demand forecasting
key_people: Dr. Jack Buffington (Director of Supply Chain & Sustainability)
short_description: First Key is a brewing and beverage industry consulting firm with more than 40 years of experience working across 50-plus countries. It advises brewers and beverage companies on strategy, finance, operations, engineering, supply chain and more. It publishes an Insights series that includes articles on how AI and big data apply to beer and beverage supply chains.

name: Arryved
ai_use_case: taproom/point-of-sale data & analytics for craft beverage operators
short_description: Arryved is a point-of-sale and operations platform built specifically for craft beverage businesses such as breweries, taprooms, cideries and distilleries. It unifies service, online ordering, production, payments and reporting into a single data model that delivers real-time, brewery-specific analytics. Its aggregate POS dataset spans more than 2,000 taprooms and is used, with the Brewers Association, to analyze industry taproom sales trends.

name: Ekos
short_description: Business-management software for craft beverage producers (breweries, wineries, cideries, distilleries, seltzer), covering inventory, production, sales and accounting with reporting on top. Serves close to 2,000 businesses on six continents. Ekos makes no public AI or machine-learning claims; it is tracked here as the system of record that brewery production data comes out of, not as an AI vendor.

name: MontBlancAI
short_description: Operational-intelligence platform that turns existing plant data into real-time insight for process manufacturers, with a dedicated brewery and distillery offering that detects fermentation deviations and flags issues before they become production losses. Ships as a module inside Ignition SCADA.

name: Symrise (SymVision)
short_description: Global flavour and fragrance house whose SymVision platform uses AI to predict taste, nutrition and health trends and steer food and beverage product development. Beverage is one of several categories it serves, not its sole focus.

name: Solera
short_description: Winery operating system spanning vineyard operations, cellar management, lab tracking, compliance, inventory, DTC and wine club in one platform, with AI built into the workflow. Covers the direct-to-consumer end of the chain that most production-focused tools stop short of.

name: Alcohol Compliance Company
short_description: AI-assisted alcohol and tobacco compliance: licensing, permitting, reporting and label approvals, with expert human review on top of the automation. Covers the regulatory layer every producer and distributor carries.

name: Wizata
short_description: Industrial AI platform for process manufacturers with a dedicated beer and beverage line, applying machine learning to optimise plant operations and the energy and utility load that comes with them.

name: Lineview
short_description: Guided manufacturing intelligence built for beverage packaging lines, targeting OEE gains and production visibility. Fills the packaging end of the chain, which sits between brewing and distribution and is thinly covered elsewhere on this radar.

name: Harmony AI
short_description: Back-office automation for beverage distributors, aimed at the order-to-cash and administrative margin leak that happens off the truck rather than on it.

name: AVEVA (PI System, formerly OSIsoft)
short_description: AVEVA sells the PI System, the operations data historian it acquired with OSIsoft in 2021, which collects, stores and contextualises real-time plant sensor data at sub-second granularity. AVEVA Predictive Analytics layers machine-learning anomaly detection on that data for early equipment-failure detection. AVEVA publishes no beer, whiskey or wine specific AI product: it is tracked here as the plant data layer that brewing and distilling analytics are built on top of, not as a beverage AI vendor.

name: Krones
ai_use_case: AI digital twins for beverage line simulation
short_description: Krones builds filling and packaging lines for breweries and beverage producers worldwide. It has moved its line simulation to digital twins with integrated AI agents, developed with NVIDIA and Microsoft, cutting simulation runs from three or four hours to under five minutes. It also ships AI on the machine itself, including an AI-equipped version of its Dynafill filler.

name: Rockwell Automation (FactoryTalk, Plex)
ai_use_case: brewery automation and MES production data
short_description: Rockwell Automation sells brewery production automation, with FactoryTalk software and the Plex manufacturing execution system unifying brewhouse, cellar and packaging data in one production ecosystem. It publishes brewery-specific automation solutions and named brewing customers including Sleeman. The brewery offer is primarily control, MES and visibility rather than machine learning, and is tracked as the operational data source under brewery analytics.

name: Siemens (Opcenter)
ai_use_case: brewing MES, R&D formulation and production scheduling
short_description: Siemens sells the Opcenter portfolio into brewing: Opcenter Execution as a brewery MES, Opcenter APS for production planning and scheduling, and Opcenter RD&L for formulated product development and laboratory management. Coopers Brewery in Australia uses Opcenter RD&L for recipe development and lab management. The value is captured manufacturing data turned into decisions rather than a specific brewing ML model.

name: AccountTouch
short_description: AccountTouch is a CRM and sales intelligence platform built specifically for beverage alcohol brands and distributors. Its AI Depletion Insights feature lets reps ask plain English questions of their depletion data instead of reading dashboards, and turns visit notes, orders and product drop-offs into a prioritised briefing per account. The AI Insights capability launched in November 2025.

name: Andavi Solutions (GreatVines)
ai_use_case: sales execution and trade promotion analytics
short_description: Andavi Solutions sells a sales execution platform for beverage alcohol suppliers and distributors, covering CRM, trade promotion management, planogram compliance, pricing and analytics, marketed as powered by AI with an AI-powered billback management module. Named customers include Diageo, Heineken, William Grant and Sons and Pabst. The GreatVines CRM is its beverage alcohol sales management product.

name: Dimensional Insight
short_description: Dimensional Insight sells analytics software to beverage alcohol distributors and suppliers through its Diver Platform, with purpose-built modules including Distributor Advisor, Supplier Advisor, Program Advisor and Inventory Advisor. It markets a Governed AI offering on top of the platform. The core product is governed BI and dashboards for beverage alcohol rather than a predictive model.

name: Dolia
ai_use_case: sales automation with natural-language data assistant
key_people: Giovanni Binello (Co-Founder), Eraldo Federico Acchiappati (Co-Founder), Andrea Aschei (Co-Founder)
short_description: Dolia is a growth platform for wine, beer and spirits producers, covering public producer profiles, distributor and agent matchmaking, digital tasting catalogues and a sales suite for orders, commissions and stock. A built-in AI assistant lets producers query their own sales data in natural language, and the platform uses AI to centralise sales processes and automate complex orders. It was the only Luxembourg company among eight finalists selected from 80 applicants for the 2026 Wine Tech Challenge.

name: Prefe
short_description: Prefe is an Italian wine tech startup that runs an instant intelligence system tracking more than 8,000 retail outlets every day, so wineries can manage distribution and pricing across large grocery chains. It was selected as one of eight finalists in the 2026 Wine Tech Challenge, an Italian open innovation programme run with major wine companies.

name: InnoVint
ai_use_case: winery production data and workflow automation
short_description: InnoVint is cloud winery management software covering vineyard tracking, wine production, inventory, cost accounting and TTB compliance reporting. It markets intelligent winery workflows and AI-assisted automation to cut administrative busywork, with clients reporting savings of 15 to 30 hours per week. The system of record is the product; the AI layer sits on top of winery operations data.

name: Vicinity Software (VicinityBrew)
short_description: Vicinity Software builds process manufacturing ERP add-ons for Microsoft Dynamics, with VicinityBrew listed on Microsoft AppSource as a brewery management app for Dynamics 365 Business Central (Essentials and Premium). It covers brewhouse and cellar operations, beer formula management, production scheduling, batch costing, quality control and TTB style compliance reporting. The company makes no public AI or machine learning claims; tracked as the system of record that brewery production and cost data comes out of.

name: CAP Vision (CAP Vignes)
short_description: CAP Vision is a French Microsoft Dynamics partner whose CAP Vignes app is published on Microsoft AppSource for Dynamics 365 Business Central. It serves winemakers, wine estates, cooperatives, wine merchants and distilleries with vinification and production management, stock tracking, DRM and customs declarations, and sales. Named customers include Bestheim, Hugel et Fils and Ethic Drinks. No public AI or machine learning claims; tracked as a wine and spirits system of record.

name: EOS Solutions (EOS WineSuite / EOS Wine)
short_description: EOS Solutions is an Italian ISV with over 100 apps on Microsoft AppSource for Dynamics 365 Business Central, including EOS Wine and the broader EOS WineSuite. The suite covers vineyard field activities, cellar operations such as cutting, transfer and sweetening, bottling production BOMs, and warehouse and finance, and is co-marketed with KUMAVISION in the DACH region. The wine modules make no public AI claims; tracked as the winery system of record on Business Central.

name: KLH Consulting (Vintegrate)
short_description: KLH Consulting is a Microsoft partner in Sonoma County that builds Vintegrate, a winery ERP layered on Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central. Modules cover winemaking and production tracking, back office operations, and a Vintegrate 360 CRM, deployed on premise or in the cloud. It makes no public AI or machine learning claims; tracked as the winery system of record that harvest, cellar and cost data lands in.

name: Aptean
funding_stage: private equity owned (TA Associates, Vista Equity, Charlesbank)
short_description: Aptean is an industry-specific ERP vendor whose Aptean Beverage ERP line, built on Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central and Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations, targets breweries, distilleries, cider makers and beverage wholesale distributors with formula management, lot traceability, excise tax and bonded warehouse handling. In 2026 it launched AppCentral, an AI platform with AI agents and process automation for Business Central customers, and it markets predictive insights and on-demand data analysis across its food and beverage suite. The AI is agent and analytics tooling layered on ERP data rather than domain sensory or process models.

name: Encompass Technologies
key_people: Jonathan O'Neil (Co-founder), Kent O'Neil (Co-founder)
short_description: Encompass Technologies builds cloud ERP for beverage producers and distributors, covering grain to glass production, accounting and compliance for breweries, distilleries and cideries, with named users including Yards Brewing, Martin House Brewing and Old Dominick Distillery. It acquired the Australian wine production platform vintrace in 2022 and vineyard software eVineyard in 2025, extending it into wineries. Its EncompassIQ suite (ApIQ, OrderIQ, ReportingIQ) and Encompass Cowork are marketed as AI-native, applying AI to accounts payable, order management and reporting on top of beverage ERP data.

name: Quantiphi (OrderSmart)
short_description: Quantiphi is an AI services firm that publishes OrderSmart on Azure Marketplace, an Azure AI based demand forecasting and predictive ordering SaaS for FMCG and beverage direct-store-delivery distributors, built in partnership with CONA Services. It ships a beer distributor edition and has presented predictive ordering to the Brewers Association, with the vendor claiming more than 10,000 sales associates using it daily and up to 60 percent reduction in per-store servicing cost. The AI is a proprietary machine learning sales forecasting model that pre-generates suggested orders for reps.

name: Vinsight
key_people: Simon Lampen (Founder)
short_description: Vinsight is a cloud production, inventory and sales platform for wineries, breweries, cideries and distilleries, built by winemaker and developer Simon Lampen in Auckland. It tracks malt and mash through fermentation and bottling, handles excise tax and traceability, chemical analysis reporting, temperature control integration and Xero accounting integration, and is used by roughly a fifth of active New Zealand wine companies. It makes no public AI or machine learning claims; tracked as a small and mid size producer system of record.

name: LiquorChat
short_description: LiquorChat is an AI platform built specifically for the alcoholic beverage trade, serving retailers, distributors and producers across wine and spirits, craft beer, RTD and non-alc. It offers in-store AI assistants grounded in a product knowledge base the vendor puts at over 500,000 beverage data points, demand forecasting and digital ordering, real-time depletion and shelf analytics, and agentic multi-agent reasoning flows. Company location, founding year and founders are not disclosed on the site, and no Microsoft or Azure relationship is stated.

name: Prosper Insights & Analytics
key_people: Gary Drenik (CEO and Co-Founder), Phil Rist (Co-Founder)
short_description: Prosper Insights & Analytics is a zero-party consumer data company that publishes pre-trained propensity models as Amazon SageMaker model packages on AWS Marketplace. Two of those listings are directly beverage-alcohol specific: Propensity-Drink Wine and Propensity-Drink Bourbon, which score the probability that a US adult drinks wine or bourbon from inputs such as gender, age range, household income and zip code. The wine model is trained on survey responses from over 17,000 US adults and reports a lift over random of 1.46. This is real supervised ML sold as a deployable model artifact, not a dashboard.

name: Alt/Finance (ALT/FNDATA)
ai_use_case: wine and whisky auction price data feed
short_description: Alt/Finance is an alternative asset data provider whose AWS Data Exchange listing Real-time & Historical Data Feeds | Global Wine & Whisky Auctions carries 20-plus years of every wine and whisky lot sold at Christie's, Sotheby's, Bonhams and Phillips from 2000 onward, 169 fields per record, roughly 2GB, updated intraday. Wine & Spirits is one of eight asset classes they track. The product itself is a normalised data feed with no machine learning in it; the only AI angle is a Claude MCP integration that lets analysts query the verified market data from an LLM client. Delivery is via AWS Data Exchange, API, Redshift materialized views, Snowflake, FactSet and FTP.

name: LikeFolio
ai_use_case: social media purchase intent and sentiment signals
key_people: Andy Swan (Co-Founder), Landon Swan (Co-Founder)
short_description: LikeFolio sells an AWS Marketplace data product called Alcoholic Beverage Companies | Purchase Intent & Consumer Sentiment, covering five listed alcohol companies (BREW, BUD, CUERVO.MX, STZ, TAP) with daily purchase intent signals, positive and negative sentiment post counts, and mention counts including slang and misspellings, back to January 2012. The signals are extracted from consumer social media text, so there is text classification underneath, but the listing does not describe the NLP or model methodology, and the company markets itself to investors rather than to producers. Priced at 1,000 USD per 12-month contract.

name: Selartag
ai_use_case: wine cellar inventory and sales advisory
key_people: Herve Lemaire (Founder and President)
short_description: Selartag is a French startup that digitises wine cellar and bottle inventory using RFID or QR smart labels, handheld and fixed portal readers, and a mobile and web app, sold to restaurants, sommeliers, wine merchants, collectors and vineyards. Its AWS architecture is documented in an AWS partner success story built with Eviden/Atos, running Lambda, EC2, RDS Postgres and Amazon Bedrock. Bedrock powers the AI features: auto-generating bottle records in one click, suggesting which wines are likely to sell based on historical data and weather, and food pairing recommendations. The case study reports inventory audits dropping from over two days to under 30 minutes and error rates from roughly 10 percent to under 1 percent.

name: BEERSOFT
ai_use_case: brewery customer service and operations agents
short_description: BEERSOFT builds custom AI and agent implementations specifically for breweries, taprooms, brewpubs and beverage brands across the US and Canada. Products include RAG systems grounded in brewery documents such as menus and policies, customer service chatbots answering taproom hours, beer availability, events and reservations, and autonomous agents that process reservations and generate reports. It integrates with brewery systems including Square, Toast and Ekos. AWS Bedrock is one of the named deployment platforms alongside OpenAI API, LangChain and Azure AI, chosen for VPC integration and enterprise security. Offices listed in Fredericton, Saint John and North Vancouver.

name: Vision33 (Brutos)
short_description: Brutos is Vision33's cloud beverage management ERP for brewers and distillers, built on SAP Business One and hosted in Vision33's own AWS environment, managed by their cloud and security specialists. It covers production, brand management, inventory and financials for manufacturers and contract packers of beer, spirits, cider, RTDs and non-alcoholic drinks, and Vision33 is a Brewers Association member. Honest read on AI: the Brutos product makes no AI or ML claim at all. Vision33 markets an AI assistant (Copilot for SAP Business One) separately, but it is not presented as part of Brutos.

name: Complexica
ai_use_case: supply and demand optimisation for beverage alcohol producers and distributors
key_people: Matthew Michalewicz (Co-CEO and co-founder), Zbigniew Michalewicz (Chief Scientist)
short_description: Complexica sells Decision Cloud, a modular enterprise platform driven by its AI and optimisation engine branded Larry, the Digital Analyst, covering demand forecasting, promotional planning, production scheduling and sales enablement. Named beverage alcohol customers on its own site include Pernod Ricard Winemakers, Asahi Beverages, Lion and liquor wholesaler Metcash. For Pernod Ricard Winemakers it went live across Australian and New Zealand wineries including Rowland Flat in the Barossa Valley, optimising winery, bottling and finished-goods planning, then extended to harvest and grape intake optimisation.

name: Commerce7
ai_use_case: wine club churn and signup prediction plus natural-language analytics
key_people: Andrew Kamphuis (President and founder)
short_description: Direct-to-consumer commerce platform used by more than 3,500 wineries, covering point of sale, wine clubs and subscriptions, ecommerce, reservations and CRM. Its predictive layer includes club churn prediction to flag members likely to cancel, club signup prediction to flag customers ready to join, and Ask Pip, a natural-language interface for querying winery data. Wine only, no beer or spirits positioning. Owned by Fullsteam, which also acquired WineDirect's SaaS division and the WinePulse analytics platform.

name: LibDib (LibTech / Supplier Cloud)
ai_use_case: ai-enhanced product content and catalog data for alcohol suppliers and distributors
key_people: Cheryl Durzy (CEO, LibDib), Richard Brashears (General Manager, LibTech)
short_description: LibDib is a web-based wholesale beverage alcohol distributor; LibTech is its SaaS division licensing the platform to other alcohol distributors. In August 2025 LibTech launched Supplier Cloud, marketed as an AI-powered content platform for beverage alcohol suppliers and distributors. The AI is content-side rather than analytics: it enriches and keeps current brand and product data across SKUs, vintages, categories and compliance requirements, and auto-generates sell sheets, digital catalogs and distributor-ready data feeds for ecommerce integration.

name: Constellation Brands
ai_use_case: bigquery ml predictive analytics for direct-to-consumer wine and spirits
key_people: Ryan Mason (Director, Head of DTC Growth and Strategy)

people.name: Ryan Mason
people.role: Director, Head of DTC Growth and Strategy

short_description: International producer and marketer of beer, wine and spirits with operations in the US, Mexico, New Zealand and Italy, including Corona, Modelo, Robert Mondavi Winery and High West Whiskey. Google Cloud published a case study on its direct-to-consumer transformation, in which Constellation runs BigQuery as the DTC data warehouse, uses BigQuery ML for predictive analytics on customer acquisition cost, lifetime value, churn and NPS, and uses Looker with LookML for modelling, reporting a 60 percent reduction in hours to reach critical decisions. The AI here is SQL-based ML on commerce data, not production or sensory AI.

name: Lion Brewery (Ceylon) PLC
ai_use_case: demand forecasting and predictive maintenance on google cloud
short_description: Sri Lanka's largest brewer, based in Biyagama. It moved its SAP system and analytics stack to Google Cloud, running BigQuery and Looker Studio Pro for reporting, and is targeting a 10 percentage point improvement in demand forecast accuracy using Google Cloud AI against weather, market and geopolitical volatility. It also plans to apply Google Cloud AI and ML services to IoT-ready brewery machines for predictive maintenance. The forecasting and maintenance AI are stated as targets and plans, so treat as pilot rather than proven production.

name: GEA Group
ai_use_case: real-time brewhouse and fermentation performance analytics
short_description: GEA is a process-equipment supplier with a dedicated brewery systems line (brewhouses, fermentation, separation) and a software product, GEA InsightPartner Brewery, that captures live process data across more than 120 parameters and flags deviations against target benchmarks during the brew rather than after it. Named brewery users include Stortebeker Braumanufaktur in Stralsund, Germany, which reported a 5 to 8 percent productivity gain in the pilot phase, plus pFriem Family Brewers and Brique House on the automation side. Honest read on the AI: InsightPartner as documented is real-time rule-based comparison and KPI benchmarking, not machine learning. GEA trade press separately promotes an OptiPartner autopilot optimisation concept with AI framing, but the brewery product pages do not substantiate ML models.

name: Augury
ai_use_case: predictive machine health on brewery packaging lines
short_description: Augury sells continuous machine-health monitoring: wireless vibration, temperature and magnetic sensors on rotating equipment feeding ML diagnostic models that classify developing faults and prescribe repairs. Heineken is named as a customer on Augury's own beverage industry page, and Augury publishes a brewery case where an alert on a filler and seamer malfunction avoided the loss of roughly 960,000 cans of beer and eight-plus hours of line downtime, plus a Top 10 global brewing company quoted on servo motor defects. This is genuine supervised ML on sensor signals, not marketing framing, though it is asset reliability rather than anything about the beer recipe or fermentation itself.

name: Ziemann Holvrieka
ai_use_case: brewery digital twin with ai-supported process recommendations
short_description: Ziemann Holvrieka builds brewhouses, tanks and process plant for breweries and sells Ziemann AnalytiX, a brewery digitalisation platform delivered in partnership with Indeex that spans brewhouse, fermentation, filtration, utilities and packaging as a process digital twin. The platform markets real-time process monitoring, automated batch tracking, recipe optimisation and what it calls AI-supported recommendations for cutting energy, water and raw material use. The vendor does not disclose the model type or publish named brewery customers for AnalytiX, so treat the AI claim as vendor-asserted rather than independently evidenced; the underlying brewery hardware and automation business is unambiguously real.

name: Endress+Hauser
ai_use_case: inline brewing process measurement and spoilage detection
short_description: Endress+Hauser runs a dedicated beer quality control practice covering inline density, flow, dissolved oxygen, conductivity and colour measurement through fermentation, maturation and filtration, plus the Fermentation Monitor QWX43 and the BioSense PCR system that identifies spoilage bacteria on the plant floor in hours instead of days. Named brewery references on its own site include Riegele, Hofbrauhaus Munich and Hacker-Pschorr. To be plain about it: this is process instrumentation and sensor-based early deviation detection, with no machine learning claimed anywhere on the brewing pages. It belongs on the radar as the measurement layer that brewery AI depends on, not as an AI vendor.

name: Emerson
ai_use_case: fermentation and distillation process measurement automation
short_description: Emerson runs separate application practices for brewing and for distilled spirits, covering milling, mashing, fermentation, stills and maturation with Rosemount instrumentation and DeltaV batch control. Vendor-hosted case studies include a whisky distillery that automated its fermentation process with the Rosemount 5408 non-contacting radar level transmitter, the University of Kentucky improving spirit blending through automated density measurement, and Vega Brewery raising plant throughput with a Rosemount 1408H level transmitter. There is no AI or machine learning claim on any of these beer or spirits pages; it is sensing, control and batch traceability.

name: Sidel
ai_use_case: packaging line performance and predictive maintenance analytics
short_description: Sidel is a filling and packaging line OEM with a large brewery installed base, including Birra Peroni's Bari plant (EvoFILL Glass filler at 50,000 bottles per hour, EvoDECO labeller, SWING pasteuriser) and Bali Hai Brewery's canning line in Indonesia. Its Evo-ON cloud suite adds Care and Performance apps that rank the machine faults causing efficiency loss and time maintenance of specific parts, with the Efficiency Improvement Tool installed at Birra Peroni for real-time line status. Sidel markets Evo-ON as having built-in intelligence and predictive capability, but its own pages describe no models or ML method, so read the predictive claim as condition-based analytics until proven otherwise.

name: SymphonyAI
ai_use_case: brewing line drift detection and root cause analysis
short_description: SymphonyAI's industrial division launched a set of eight AI applications built specifically for CPG food and beverage plants, and its own announcement calls out brewing by name: full 3D modelling of brewing, thermal processing, canning, packaging and utilities for throughput simulation. The apps target high-speed lines, thermal variability, CIP and SIP complexity and micro-stoppages, combining domain models with causal reasoning to catch drift and surface root cause before yield or quality slips. Caveat: no named brewery customer has been published and the release does not identify the underlying models beyond the Microsoft Foundry and Azure stack, so this is a credible brewing-targeted product with unproven brewery deployments.

name: Evocon
short_description: Evocon is a cloud OEE and production monitoring product that pulls machine signals automatically and visualises availability, performance and quality losses per line. Its published brewery customer is Kalnapilis, a Lithuanian brewery in the Royal Unibrew group running four shifts around the clock, which uses Evocon for real-time line monitoring, shift handover and production scheduling. There is no AI or machine learning in this product; it is automated data collection, downtime reason coding and dashboards. Included because it is a verified, named brewery deployment of a production data layer, not because it is an AI vendor.

name: TeepTrak
ai_use_case: filling line micro-stop and oee monitoring
short_description: TeepTrak sells retrofit OEE and performance monitoring hardware plus software and publishes a dedicated brewery operations page describing filling-line micro-stop analysis, with an example of a mid-size brewery halving filling-line downtime by adjusting rates and preventive maintenance off the real-time data. The brewery example is anonymised, so the evidence here is an explicit brewing product page rather than a named customer. The core product is monitoring and analytics with no ML; TeepTrak lists machine learning separately as a complementary offering under a jemba.ai link, which is not part of the brewery case described.

name: Rare Whisky 101
ai_use_case: rare whisky market data and valuation
short_description: Rare Whisky 101 runs a valuation and market-intelligence service for rare single malt Scotch, selling valuations to collectors, insurers, banks, solicitors and estates. Its own site reports a database of over 1.6 million records covering 235 distilleries and 90,306 bottles, from which it publishes secondary-market indices such as the Icon 100. There is no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on the site; this is a curated auction-price dataset plus human expert valuation, and it belongs in the radar as a spirits market-data company rather than an AI company.

name: WhiskyInvestDirect
ai_use_case: maturing scotch exchange and market data
short_description: WhiskyInvestDirect operates a live 24/7 order-board exchange where private investors buy and sell maturing Scotch by the litre of pure alcohol, held in bonded warehouses. It publishes genuine market data: live and historical prices, monthly audited stock and ownership registers, and distillery-by-quarter volume tables that few other sources make public. It states it holds roughly 36 million bottles equivalent for about 5,000 users. The platform does not run predictive models or AI; its value in this database is as an open source of spirits market data.

name: SipSource
ai_use_case: machine learning demand forecasting for spirits and wine
short_description: SipSource is the wine and spirits market-data and forecasting product of the Wholesalers and Distributors of America (WSWA), built from single-product depletion transactions between wholesalers and retailers across all 50 US states. Its own site states the forecasting product is powered by advanced machine learning, with models combining distributor depletions and macroeconomic indicators such as inflation, unemployment and consumer confidence. Subscribers get segment, price-tier and channel breakdowns for spirits categories including whiskey.

name: Ai Palette
ai_use_case: flavour and consumer trend prediction for drinks product development
short_description: Ai Palette runs an AI consumer-insights platform for food and drink companies, with three products: Foresight Engine for emerging trend detection, Concept Genie for AI product-concept generation and Screen Winner for virtual concept validation. Its models sit on 61 billion data points from search, social and e-retail across 24 countries and 18 languages. Diageo is a named client, using the platform to track health and wellness trends in beverage alcohol to steer R and D; it is also the vendor behind Diageo flavour-forecasting work. Offices in Singapore, Bengaluru and New York; now part of GlobalData.

name: Endless West
ai_use_case: molecular spirit formulation from analytical chemistry data
short_description: Endless West makes spirits molecularly rather than by barrel ageing. It uses analytical chemistry, mainly GC-MS style profiling, to identify the compounds responsible for whiskey aroma and flavour, sources those molecules from other natural feedstocks and rebuilds a target profile from ethanol upward in under 24 hours. Its whiskey-inspired brand Glyph launched in 2018 and it now sells bulk spirit, concentrates, private label and co-packing. To be plain, the differentiator is compound-level chemistry and a proprietary flavour library, not a published machine learning model.

name: FIVE x 5 Solutions
ai_use_case: distillery production data and ttb compliance analytics
short_description: FIVE x 5 Solutions builds craft distillery management software, sold as DISTILL x 5 and Whiskey Systems, covering production tracking, barrel and inventory records and TTB and Canadian excise reporting for American and Canadian distillers. It adds a business intelligence layer over that production data for yield, loss and cost reporting. No AI or machine learning is claimed on the site; it is a distilling data and compliance platform.

name: Spirit Sight
ai_use_case: barrel maturation analytics and angel's share forecasting
short_description: Spirit Sight is barrel management and distillery operations software for American whiskey producers, tracking each cask by serial, lot, mashbill, fill and dump date, entry and current proof, volume, location and live value. Its differentiator is a live 3D rickhouse view with gap detection and temperature and humidity heatmaps, plus per-barrel evaporative loss tracking that turns angel's share into a forecastable cost feeding valuation and TTB reporting. The analytics are statistical and sensor driven rather than machine learning.

name: CaskX
ai_use_case: cask valuation from distillery and auction comparables
short_description: CaskX sells bourbon barrel and Scotch cask ownership to private investors and runs periodic valuations of client holdings. Its stated method is comparables based: current sales data by distillery, region, vintage and cask type is assembled into an estimated market value. Offices in Los Angeles, Louisville, London, Toronto, Sydney and Hong Kong. There is no machine learning here, and no independently audited index; it is a broker with an internal valuation dataset, which is worth stating plainly given how often cask investment marketing implies more.

name: WhiskyCircle
ai_use_case: ai whisky sommelier and taste profile recommendations
short_description: WhiskyCircle is a Dutch consumer whisky platform, described by early coverage as a Vivino for whisky, that launched iOS and Android apps in April 2026. Users log tastings, rate bottles on a 1 to 5 scale in 0.25 steps, track collections and follow festivals and tastings. Its own site fronts an AI sommelier called Isla that reads a user's rating history to build a taste profile and recommend bottles. Catalogue is reported at over 33,000 whiskies across 1,200 distilleries.

name: IES (Integrated Environmental Solutions)
ai_use_case: distillery digital twin for energy and waste heat optimisation
short_description: IES builds physics-based digital twins of buildings and manufacturing sites. In a distillery project it pulled existing meter and process data into its iSCAN platform, used AI and machine learning to fill data gaps and disaggregate utility bills into granular time-series profiles, then simulated interventions in a 3D model of the plant. The twin quantified that waste heat recovery could meet 5 percent of heating demand and solar PV 4.1 percent of electricity, for 6.9 percent CO2 savings. Relevant to distilling decarbonisation, which is now a live pressure on Scotch producers.

name: AI4Whisky
ai_use_case: carbon footprint modelling for single malt production
key_people: Shiwen Zhuang (Researcher, ICBD Heriot-Watt), Annie Hill (Professor of Brewing and Distilling)
short_description: AI4Whisky is a free web tool from the International Centre for Brewing and Distilling at Heriot-Watt University that calculates the carbon footprint of single malt Scotch production across the distillery, maturation warehouse and bottling hall, covering Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions including raw materials, transport and waste. A published case study on a 3,000 LPA batch distillery returned 2.83 kg CO2e per 70 cl bottle, with Scope 3 accounting for 77 percent. Despite the name it is a life cycle assessment calculator, not a machine learning model.

name: Cropsy Technologies
ai_use_case: vine-by-vine computer vision scanning for disease, yield and pruning counts
key_people: Ali Alomari (Co-founder), Leila Deljkovic (Co-founder), Winston Su (Co-founder), Rory Buchanan (Co-founder)
short_description: Cropsy mounts camera scanners on tractors, harvesters and ATVs that profile individual grapevines as the vehicle drives through the block, up to 8,000 vines per scanner per hour. On-board AI tags each vine and returns disease detection, cane and bud counts, missing-vine maps and yield estimates through its Osiris software. This is genuine computer vision inference running at the edge, not just sensor logging. Customers named on its own site include Cloudy Bay and Martell.

name: Chouette
ai_use_case: drone imagery analysis for vine disease and vigour mapping
short_description: Chouette builds its own drones plus an image-analysis pipeline for precision viticulture, selling a complete capture-and-analysis service to winegrowers in France. Its own site states the offer combines artificial intelligence with agronomic expertise, trained on millions of vineyard images captured at millimetre precision, to produce vigour maps, disease detection and spray volume recommendations. Kubota Corporation invested in the company in 2023.

name: Fruition Sciences
ai_use_case: vine water status and grape maturation prediction from sap flow and climate data
key_people: Sebastien Payen (Co-founder), Thibaut Scholasch (Co-founder)
short_description: Fruition Sciences runs a vineyard monitoring platform that links climate, irrigation, soil maps, fertilisation and plant development data to fruit maturation, delivered as cloud and mobile software for winemakers. In-vine sap flow sensors report every 15 minutes and proprietary algorithms compute reference evapotranspiration, plant transpiration and vine stress. The company states on its own site that it applies machine learning techniques alongside plant physiology and GIS expertise to generate predictive alerts. Montpellier is the French base, with a second office in Napa, California.

name: PlantVoice
ai_use_case: grapevine stress and disease prediction from in-trunk sap biosensors
key_people: Matteo Beccatelli (CEO and Co-founder), Tommaso Beccatelli (Head of Production, Co-founder), Pierluigi Lodi Rizzini (Legal, Co-founder)
short_description: PlantVoice makes a toothpick-sized biocompatible biosensor inserted into the plant stem that analyses sap in real time, paired with cloud software that classifies stress signatures. Its own site claims AI-based software processing the physiological signal, with stated accuracy of 94 percent for forecasts and 97 percent for stress identification. Vineyards are a core crop, with named grapevine deployments at Italian wineries Cantina Mezzacorona and Cantina Cavit, and it was one of eight startups selected for the 2026 Wine Tech Challenge in Verona. It also covers kiwi, apple and peach, so it is not wine-only.

name: Vinhood
ai_use_case: consumer taste profiling and wine recommendation
total_raised: About 3 million EUR round led by Linfa (Riello Investimenti Sgr)
short_description: Vinhood runs a taste-profiling engine that builds a Taste Identity from a sub-one-minute questionnaire about food habits, then recommends wines, beers and coffees against that profile. It sells the engine B2B to brands and retailers as a personalisation layer and runs a consumer app. The recommendation engine is branded Virtual Sommelier and the company reports roughly 80 percent accuracy validated against 500-plus tasting sessions and university studies. Honest read on the AI: this is a validated sensory-science recommendation algorithm, and the company does not publicly document machine learning models.

name: Elaisian
ai_use_case: vineyard disease forecasting and irrigation decision support
short_description: Elaisian is an agronomic decision support system combining weather stations, satellite data and predictive models to tell growers when to treat, irrigate and fertilise. Its vineyard module forecasts powdery mildew, downy mildew, botrytis and vine moth pressure ahead of visible symptoms. The company reports 50,000 hectares monitored across 20 countries and roughly 4,000 farms. It began in olive growing and vineyards are one crop among several, so it is not a wine-only company.

name: Agricolus
ai_use_case: satellite vigour mapping and phytopathology forecast models for vineyards
short_description: Agricolus is an Italian precision farming platform combining satellite crop monitoring, weather station and sensor integration, scouting apps and prescription maps, with viticulture as a supported crop. Its own site cites winery customers such as Cantina Roccafiore using chlorophyll and vigour indices to find vineyard water stress, and reports 2.3 million satellite images processed across 104 countries. Honest read on the AI: the platform advertises phenology, irrigation, insect and phytopathy forecast models, which are agronomic simulation models, and it does not publicly document machine learning.

name: BitMetrics
ai_use_case: computer vision quality inspection of wine during bottling
key_people: Mar Masulli (CEO)
short_description: BitMetrics is a Barcelona deep-tech company building vision-guided robotics and AI visual inspection software (Pick+ and Scan+) for industrial lines. Its wine application is the VINIA project with Familia Torres, where image sensors and machine learning models spin each bottle to detect and isolate foreign particles in the wine during bottling, piloted at the Torres winery in Pacs del Penedes. The project received about 29,000 EUR of ACCIO innovation funding. Wine is one vertical inside a broader industrial automation business.

name: Wine Services
ai_use_case: wine and spirits market, pricing and distribution intelligence
short_description: Wine Services is a Bordeaux-based market intelligence platform tracking on-trade and off-trade distribution, pricing and competitive placement for wine and spirits brands. Its own site reports 805,000 wines and spirits tracked, 100,000 points of sale, and coverage of 105 markets across more than 25 countries, used by over 250 brands. Honest read on the AI: this is a data-collection and SaaS analytics business rather than an ML business, and the AI feature it advertises is an MCP server letting customers pipe the market dataset into Claude, Codex and custom agents.

name: TerraClim
ai_use_case: vineyard climate and terroir intelligence mapping
short_description: TerraClim describes itself on its own site as climate intelligence for vineyards, orchards and consultants, delivering fine-scale climate and terroir data to South African wine and fruit growers. It grew from a Stellenbosch university spin-off into an industry tool funded and supported by South Africa Wine, which won a 2026 Western Cape Economy Innovation Award for backing it. Honest read on the AI: this is spatial climate modelling and a decision-support data layer, with no publicly documented machine learning.

name: VIP (Vermont Information Processing)
ai_use_case: distributor pricing, predictive ordering and conversational reporting
short_description: VIP builds route accounting, ecommerce, pricing and analytics software used across the beverage alcohol three tier system (beer, wine and spirits suppliers, distributors and retailers). In July 2026 it launched VIP Intelligence, a bundle of AI features: AI-powered revenue management inside PriceStream, AI Predictive Order in Connect and the VIP Sales App, and natural language AI reporting in iDIG. The underlying products are mature route accounting and BI systems, so the AI is a prediction and language layer on top of an existing transactional data estate rather than a new modelling company.

name: Provi
key_people: Taylor Katzman (Founder and CEO)
short_description: Provi is the largest B2B online marketplace for beverage alcohol, connecting bars, restaurants and retailers with distributors and brands across beer, wine and spirits. It merged with SevenFifty in 2022. Provi rebuilt its search and recommendation stack on machine learning, adding personalised carousels, improved search suggestions and product discovery ranking for buyers. The ML is applied to marketplace discovery and support chat; the core business is transactional ordering, not modelling.

name: LiquidRails
ai_use_case: dtc ecommerce inventory and purchase order recommendations
short_description: LiquidRails is a direct to consumer ecommerce platform built specifically for beverage alcohol brands, handling compliant online sales and shipping to 46 plus states, payments, retail fulfilment and marketing. Its AI layer aggregates data from Shopify, ShipStation, carriers and POS systems and generates purchase order suggestions from sell through rates, low stock alerts and pricing and inventory planning recommendations. This is applied analytics and rules plus forecasting on commerce data; no distinctive proprietary model is claimed.

name: AccelPay
ai_use_case: order routing and marketing automation for alcohol dtc
short_description: AccelPay provides commerce infrastructure that lets alcohol brands sell direct from their own websites while staying inside the three tier system, routing each order to a licensed retailer in its network and handling age verification, payments and last mile delivery. It says it serves over 400 alcohol brands and offers native Shopify and iframe embeds. The AI content is modest: algorithmic order routing plus AI marketing automation and AI search visibility tooling. There is no evidence of substantive proprietary ML.

name: WISK
ai_use_case: invoice extraction and par based ordering for bars and taprooms
short_description: WISK is a beverage led inventory platform for bars, taprooms and restaurant groups covering inventory counts, invoicing, purchasing, recipe costing and COGS, with 60 plus POS integrations. Its AI is invoice scanning and extraction that updates cost of goods automatically, plus smart ordering that recommends purchases from sales data and PAR levels. The document extraction is real machine learning; the ordering logic is closer to statistical par optimisation than to a demand forecasting model.

name: Vistaar Technologies
ai_use_case: price and revenue management for the alcohol value chain
short_description: Vistaar sells pricing and revenue management software with a dedicated beverage alcohol practice, covering price structure management across producer, distributor and retail tiers, excise tax and TTB compliance, rebates, chargebacks and trade promotion optimisation. Its AI components are SherloQ, an insight suite that surfaces pricing patterns in customer data, and SmartPricingEngine, with elasticity modelling and demand forecasting behind scenario planning. Alcohol is one vertical among several for the company, so the models are general revenue management applied to bev alc constraints.

name: Next Glass
ai_use_case: consumer consumption data analytics and generative menu design
short_description: Next Glass is the parent of Untappd, Untappd for Business, Untappd Insights, Oznr, Ekos and Ollie, giving it both brewery production software and the largest consumer beer consumption dataset, over 1.5 billion logged check ins. Untappd Insights sells that data back to breweries, distributors and retailers as reports, dashboards and custom analyses covering style and flavour trends, regional consumption and sentiment. The verified AI is narrower than the data asset suggests: a generative AI design tool for digital menus in Untappd for Business, with trend work still largely aggregate analytics rather than published predictive models.

name: PourMyBeer
ai_use_case: self pour taproom pour level sales analytics
key_people: Josh Goodman (Founder and CEO)
short_description: PourMyBeer supplies self serve tap walls, stations and trailers for taprooms, breweries, hotels and stadiums, with pay by the ounce dispensing via QR, RFID or card, and gives operators pour level sales and customer behaviour reporting. Coca-Cola European Partners Ventures has invested. Honest read on the AI: the site mentions predictive analytics in its reporting but publishes no evidence of actual machine learning, so treat this as high quality pour telemetry and dashboards rather than an AI product.

name: Brewers Association (Barley assistant)
ai_use_case: retrieval assistant over brewing technical and regulatory resources
short_description: The Brewers Association, the US craft brewing trade body, launched Barley in February 2026, a chat assistant that answers member questions about brewing techniques, industry data, legislative updates and regulatory guidance. It is deliberately constrained to Brewers Association content rather than the open web, and improves through thumbs up and down feedback from members. Technically this is a retrieval assistant over a curated corpus, not novel brewing ML, but it is a notable signal of institutional AI adoption in craft beer.
